question: Can I get loan to get admission in Sanjivani University?

v1.answer: Education loans can be availed for Sanjivani University courses through participating banks on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal. Specific benefits like the 3% interest subvention depend on whether the institution meets the current NIRF QHEI eligibility criteria.
v1.follow_up: Check the institution search tool at pmvidyalaxmi.co.in to verify your course listing.

v2.answer: Yes, education loans under the IBA Model Scheme are available for students securing admission to Sanjivani University. question: Can I get loan for diploma?

v1.answer: Yes, you can get an education loan for diploma programs. Professional and technical diplomas recognized by regulatory bodies qualify under both PM-Vidyalaxmi (at eligible QHEIs) and PM-USP CSIS (with full interest subsidy if income is under Rs. 4.5 lakh).
v1.follow_up: Would you like to know the required documents to apply for a diploma education loan?

v2.answer: Yes, loans for diploma courses are eligible under government schemes. Under PM-Vidyalaxmi, all degree and diploma programs offered by designated QHEIs qualify for collateral-free education loans. Under PM-USP CSIS, professional and technical diploma programs recognized by AICTE/State Technical Boards qualify for full interest subvention during the moratorium period if family income is up to Rs. 4.5 lakh.

question: What is the income limit for 3% interest subvention under PM-Vidyalaxmi?

v1.answer: Under PM-Vidyalaxmi, students with an annual gross family income of up to Rs. 8 lakh are eligible for a 3% interest subvention on education loans up to Rs. 10 lakh during the moratorium period (course duration + 1 year). This benefit is capped at 1 lakh meritorious students per year.

question: What documents need to be uploaded on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal?

v1.answer: The mandatory documents for PM-Vidyalaxmi application are: (1) Marksheets of Class X and Class XII/qualifying examination, (2) Official admission letter/proof from the institution, (3) Detailed schedule of course fees/expenses, (4) Income certificate issued by a designated government authority (e.g. Tehsildar/SDM), (5) Aadhaar card, and (6) Passport-size photographs of the student and parent/co-applicant.
v1.follow_up: Ensure documents are in PDF or JPEG format under 200 KB each before uploading.

question: How is the moratorium period defined for education loan repayment?

v1.answer: The moratorium period (repayment holiday) is defined as the Course Duration plus 1 year. During this entire period, students are not required to pay principal EMIs. The government provides 100% interest subsidy for income <= Rs. 4.5 lakh (CSIS) or 3% interest subvention for income <= Rs. 8 lakh at a QHEI (PM-Vidyalaxmi).
v1.follow_up: Repayment of the loan begins after the moratorium ends, with a tenure of up to 15 years.

question: Is it mandatory to have an existing bank account to apply on the portal?

v1.answer: No, an existing bank account at the selected bank is not required to submit an application on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal. Once the education loan is sanctioned, the bank will open a savings account for disbursement and eventual repayment.
v1.follow_up: You can apply to up to three preferred member banks simultaneously through the single portal form.

question: Which loan I should apply for less than 5 lakh income?

v1.answer: For family income below Rs. 5 lakh, if your income is up to Rs. 4.5 lakh you qualify for PM-USP CSIS (100% interest subsidy). If your income is between Rs. 4.5 lakh and Rs. 5 lakh, you qualify for PM-Vidyalaxmi 3% interest subvention (income up to Rs. 8 lakh).
v1.follow_up: Check your income certificate to determine if you qualify for full or 3% interest subvention.

For a family income under Rs. 5 lakh, here is the best scheme pathway:
1. If income is <= Rs. 4.5 lakh: Apply for PM-USP CSIS to get 100% full interest subsidy on loans up to Rs. 10 lakh during the moratorium.
2. If income is between Rs. 4.5 lakh and Rs. 5 lakh: Apply for PM-Vidyalaxmi (income ceiling up to Rs. 8 lakh) to get a 3% interest subvention during the moratorium at eligible QHEIs.
Both schemes provide collateral-free loans backed by government credit guarantees.
